title: On Touching the rail with one finger
subtitle: 情感心理 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 情感心理（人与自我·做人与做事·情绪与心理）
meta: 主题语境：情感心理（人与自我·做人与做事·情绪与心理）　|　核心词汇：touch　|　正文 344 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 touch 的形式与含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1961 the trader ① touched the rail with one finger at once, and every partner in the market said it was the first time anybody had done such a thing there. Three weeks on, people still spoke of how quietly it was done and of how, ever since, the trader ② touches the rail with one finger in the rain without being asked. My mother said later that to ③ touch the rail with one finger at all was the part nobody had expected.

By then somebody had surely ④ touched the rail with one finger before — a line in the list for October 1955 hints at it — but nobody could name the person. ⑤ Touching the rail with one finger at once, the trader said once, is nine parts patience and one part nerve; it is not the doing of it that people remember.

My uncle, who kept the basket at the far stall, meant the other thing entirely. He said that if anybody should ever ⑥ touch everybody who heard the tale in the rain, nobody should do it twice or speak of it again. The rule the old hands handed down was plainer still: ⑦ Touch everybody who heard the tale at once and never mention it again.

By 1968 the whole business had shrunk to half a line in the list, and a new partner from the next market ⑧ touches everybody who heard the tale at once every week without once asking what it had cost the first time. My mother, who had watched all of it from the stall, said nothing at all; she simply ⑨ touched the rail with one finger again when nobody else would.

⑩ To touch the rail with one finger, my mother said in 1973, is not one thing but two: what you do and what the market remembers of it. She said the second half never grows lighter, and nowadays, whenever the market forgets, somebody touches the rail with one finger in the rain again and somebody must touch the rail with one finger at once all over again.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请为文中十处画线形式选择对应的用法说明。
options: A. v. 触摸（一般过去式 touched the rail with one finger：1961 年货商头一回这样做，二话不说地）
B. v. 触摸（一般现在 touches the rail with one finger：自那以后成了老习惯，不必有人开口）
C. v. 触摸（不定式 to touch the rail with one finger：文中两处，一是母亲说的“难就难在……”，一是结尾那句格言）
D. v. 触摸（过去完成时 had touched the rail with one finger：1955 年十月的货单上那行字之前就有人做过）
E. v. 触摸（动名词 touching the rail with one finger 作主语：“九分耐心、一分胆气”那一句）
F. v. 触动（touch everybody who heard the tale：should ever 之后的原形，指万一真要去触动每一个听到这段故事的人）
G. v. 触动（touch everybody who heard the tale：祈使句，转述老手们当年立下的那条规矩）
H. v. 触摸（后段两处：新来的伙计照例 touches everybody who heard the tale，而母亲又一次 touched the rail with one finger）

touch 意为“触摸”，自那以后货商淋着雨把这件事做了一遍又一遍，不必有人开口，故用一般现在 touches。
touch 意为“触摸”，母亲说的是“难就难在肯触摸用一个指头碰了碰栏杆”，此处为不定式 to touch the rail with one finger。
touch 意为“触摸”，货单里 十月 那行字说明早在 1968 年之前就有人触摸过，故用过去完成时 had touched。
touch 意为“触摸”，货商说“触摸用一个指头碰了碰栏杆这件事是九分耐心一分胆气”，此处 touching the rail with one finger 作主语。
touch 意为“触动”，叔叔说的是“万一真有人去触动每一个听到这段故事的人”，should ever 之后用原形 touch everybody who heard the tale。
touch 意为“触动”，老手们留下的规矩是祈使句：立刻触动每一个听到这段故事的人（touch everybody who heard the tale at once），以后再也不要提起。
touch 意为“触摸”，新来的伙计每个星期都照例触动每一个听到这段故事的人，从不问头一回的代价，用一般现在 touches。
touch 意为“触摸”，母亲在无人肯做的时候又一次二话不说地触摸用一个指头碰了碰栏杆，用一般过去式 touched 叙述。
touch 意为“触摸”，结尾那句是母亲 1973 年的话：要触摸用一个指头碰了碰栏杆，其实不是一件事，而是两件事——你做的那一件，和集市记住的那一件。

task3.title: Task 3　语境写作
task3.intro: 请写 5—6 个句子，至少使用 touch 的 3 种不同形式（过去式、第三人称、-ing、不定式等）；至少使用下列词语中的 3 个。
answers: In 1961 the trader touched the rail with one finger at once, and nobody in the market forgot it.
Even now the trader touches the rail with one finger in the rain whenever the market asks.
Touching the rail with one finger at once, my mother used to say, is nine parts patience and one part nerve.
If anybody should ever touch everybody who heard the tale in the rain, nobody should do it twice or speak of it again.
A new partner from the next market touches everybody who heard the tale at once every week, asking nothing about the past.
When nobody else would, my mother touched the rail with one finger again, and the market remembered that half.
